standard_prerequisites.name: The regular-model situation, the numerical invariants of the components and the Euler characteristic of a curve
standard_prerequisites.statement: The situation fixes a discrete valuation ring, a smooth projective curve over its fraction field, a regular proper model and the irreducible components of the special fibre with their multiplicities; the component carries a residue field, a genus and a self-intersection number, all recorded by the numerical type. The Euler characteristic of a coherent sheaf on a proper scheme over a field is additive in short exact sequences and, for a family of curves, its value is locally constant in the geometric sense; on a reduced curve it equals the difference between the dimension of the zeroth and first cohomology. The author's own definitions and lemmas of the chapter and the quoted results of the Perfect and Varieties chapters are the allowed inputs.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted lemma is the formula relating the genus of the curve to the numerical type of the special fibre, and the chapter's later comparisons of genera of different models are applications of it.

core_obligations: Write the genus of the curve through the Euler characteristic: the genus of a smooth projective curve over the fraction field is one minus the Euler characteristic of its structure sheaf, so the whole computation may be carried out on the special fibre, whose Euler characteristic agrees with that of the generic fibre by the local constancy of the Euler characteristic in a family (source lines 5168-5175).

Decompose along the components: the multiplicities give the relation between the structure sheaf of the special fibre and those of its components, and the additivity of the Euler characteristic turns the genus into a sum over the components together with correction terms coming from the pairwise intersections (source lines 5175-5195).

Identify the correction terms: for each pair of distinct components the contribution is computed from the length of the scheme-theoretic intersection, which is the intersection number, and the self-intersection appears with the sign recorded in the statement; the summand for each component therefore takes the form displayed in the lemma (source lines 5195-5215).
Assemble the formula: adding the contribution of the multiplicities and the constant term one gives exactly the expression asserted, which completes the proof (source lines 5215-5219).

proof_roadmap.step: Pass from the genus of the curve to the Euler characteristic of the special fibre by local constancy.
Use additivity and the multiplicities to decompose the Euler characteristic along the components.
Identify the correction terms with the intersection numbers of the components.
Collect the terms into the asserted formula.
